metadata.title: European Stroke Organisation (ESO), European Association of Neurosurgical Societies (EANS) and European Society for Minimally Invasive Neurological Therapy (ESMINT) guideline on aneurysmal subarachnoid haemorrhage
top_takeaways: Oral administration of nimodipine is recommended for patients with aneurysmal subarachnoid haemorrhage (aSAH).
Regular coiling is recommended over clipping if both treatment options are equally suitable for patients in good clinical condition.
Routine use of antifibrinolytic drugs, tirilazad, statins, magnesium sulphate, or endothelin receptor antagonists is not recommended.

recommendations.statement: Oral administration of nimodipine is recommended for patients with aSAH.
recommendations.verbatim_quote: Oral administration of nimodipine is recommended for patients with aSAH.

recommendations.statement: Regular coiling is recommended over clipping if both aneurysm treatment options are equally suitable in patients who are in good clinical condition.
recommendations.target_population: Patients with aSAH in good clinical condition with equally suitable treatment options
recommendations.verbatim_quote: Regular coiling is recommended over clipping if both aneurysm treatment options are equally suitable in patients who are in good clinical condition.

recommendations.statement: Routine use of antifibrinolytic drugs prior to aneurysm treatment is not recommended.
recommendations.target_population: Patients with aSAH prior to aneurysm treatment
recommendations.verbatim_quote: Routine use of antifibrinolytic drugs prior to aneurysm treatment is not recommended.

recommendations.statement: The use of tirilazad, statins, magnesium sulphate or endothelin receptor antagonists is not recommended for patients with aSAH.
recommendations.verbatim_quote: The use of tirilazad, statins, magnesium sulphate or endothelin receptor antagonists is not recommended for patients with aSAH.
